blockers.title: Processing Frames dialog: remember the window size

acceptance.check: starTests ProcessingModalAlignmentPreferenceTests.testTheChartsAreOffWhenNeverChosen: empty prefs decode → showsAlignmentInProcessingWindow == false (fails before the change, where the effective default was true).
star-desktop LocalPreferencesTest theProcessingWindowsAlignmentChartsAreOffUntilTurnedOn: assertFalse(LocalPreferences().showAlignmentInProcessingWindow) with no prefs file.
gui testTheChoiceRoundTrips (true and false, raw and effective) and the desktop test's true-then-false write/read-back both pass.
Review: LocalPreferences.kt KDoc says off until turned on; UserPreferences.swift doc comment says nil means no.

approach: gui/star/UserPreferences.swift: add a computed `var showsAlignmentInProcessingWindow: Bool { showAlignmentInProcessingWindow ?? false }` next to the optional (line ~154) so the effective default is testable without the view; correct its doc comment 'nil means yes' to 'nil means no' (line ~149).
gui/star/ProcessingModalView.swift:56: the Binding getter reads that computed property (i.e. `?? false`) instead of `?? true`; setter unchanged.
star-desktop/.../data/LocalPreferences.kt:135: `bool("showAlignmentInProcessingWindow") ?: false`; rewrite the KDoc at line 131 from 'On unless turned off' to 'Off until turned on'.

star-desktop LocalPreferencesTest.kt:229-235: rename to ...AreOffUntilTurnedOn, assertFalse on the default, then set true and read true back (proves a saved true is honoured), then set false and read false (existing assertions), keeping the file-contents check under the macOS key.

gui/starTests/starTests.swift ProcessingModalAlignmentPreferenceTests: add testTheChartsAreOffWhenNeverChosen decoding `{"recentlyOpenedSequencelist":{}}` and asserting `showsAlignmentInProcessingWindow == false`; extend testTheChoiceRoundTrips to also assert the computed property equals `chosen` for true and false (A3). Decode only, never assign (setters write the real prefs file).
Update the desktop AlignmentSection KDoc in ProcessingModal.kt only if it states the default (it does not today, so likely no change). No catalogue strings change, so no localization work.

findings.claim: Binding getter uses `showAlignmentInProcessingWindow ?? true`, so unset means charts shown.
`showAlignmentInProcessingWindow: Bool?` with didSet save; doc comment above says 'nil means yes'.
Existing test only asserts the raw optional is nil when the key is absent; nothing tests the effective default. testTheChoiceRoundTrips (2762-2777) decodes/encodes true and false.
Getter is `bool("showAlignmentInProcessingWindow") ?: true`; KDoc at 131 says 'On unless turned off'.
assertTrue on the default, then round-trips false only; after the flip the false round-trip alone would no longer prove a saved value is honoured, so it must also round-trip true.
Desktop checkbox initial state is `app.prefs.showAlignmentInProcessingWindow`, so changing the LocalPreferences default is sufficient for the desktop UI.
Demo script already says to toggle Show alignment results on to show the graphs, which matches off-by-default; no change needed.
No Gherkin feature references the show-alignment toggle (grep of gherkin/features for alignment shows only menu/settings-tab/ground-alignment steps).

plan.parity_reason: The same preference key and default flip in the gui (ProcessingModalView/UserPreferences) and the desktop (LocalPreferences), each with its own test.
risks: gui tests must decode, not assign, UserPreferences: setters write the real ~/ preferences file.
Desktop ProcessingModal reads the pref once via remember{}; no behaviour change there beyond the new initial value.
plan.summary: Flip the effective default of the processing modal's "Show alignment results" toggle (preference showAlignmentInProcessingWindow) from on to off when never saved, in both the macOS gui and the desktop client; saved values are untouched.

existing_to_extend: gui/starTests/starTests.swift ProcessingModalAlignmentPreferenceTests.testTheChoiceRoundTrips: also assert the effective computed property equals the saved true/false (A3)
star-desktop LocalPreferencesTest: the flipped test also writes true and reads it back before the existing false round-trip (A3)
